intro.text: The crown grinds against something that is not rock. When the dust settles, a steel capsule the size of a coffin hangs half out of the shaft wall, stenciled in Cyrillic. Inside, wrapped in oilcloth: a field recorder and twelve reels of tape. Reel seven is marked in red pencil. {crew} reads the stamp aloud: [[kola_well:Kola SG-3, 12 262 m]].
intro.radio: Auger, TOPSIDE. If that is Soviet hardware, it is not ours to listen to. Bag it.

logs.text: Mostly drilling chatter, and a man counting depths in a flat voice. Between counts, someone has spliced in pages of seismic logs read aloud. {crew} copies them down by hand. They map the next stretch of rock better than your own instruments do.

answer.text: At twelve thousand meters the counting stops. What follows is a long, low note, like a bow drawn across a steel cable. Then the same note again, much closer, from under the deck plates. Everyone hears it. Nobody says so.

strip.text: The capsule walls are good Soviet steel, a hand thick. Two hours with the cutting torch turns them into hull plate. The recorder goes over the side with the slag. Somewhere in an archive, a box is now empty.

leave.text: You log the position, photograph the stencils and drill on. TOPSIDE acknowledges with a single click.
